Agent Name: WomenInComputerScienceHistory_Expert
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The agent made a factual error by assuming the "final year" for the statistic was 2022 based on the search results, whereas the source text explicitly states "Today, it's only 24%" in the context of a 2016 report (referenced in Search Result 4 and 6) or implies a much more recent date ("Today" relative to the conversation). The search results actually contain a contradiction: Search Result 9 mentions "1995 2017 2022 37 %24 %22 %", suggesting the 24% figure might be associated with 2017 or that the 22% is the 2022 figure. However, the primary error is the calculation logic. The problem asks for the time to change by 13% from 37%. The search results consistently cite the 37% to 24% drop as occurring between 1995 and "Today" (which in the context of the specific Girls Who Code report cited in the search results, often refers to the 2016 Accenture report or the 2017 data point where the drop was highlighted). The correct answer provided in the prompt is 22 years. 1995 + 22 = 2017. The agent incorrectly identified the end year as 2022 (calculating 27 years) instead of 2017, likely misinterpreting the "2022" mentioned in the URL or title of Search Result 9 as the data year for the 24% figure, when the 24% figure in the specific GWC narrative usually corresponds to the 2017 data point (or the agent simply guessed 2022 as "today" without verifying the specific data year associated with the 24% stat in the source text). The search result 9 snippet "1995 2017 2022 37 %24 %22 %" strongly implies the sequence: 1995 (37%), 2017 (24%), 2022 (22%). The agent missed this sequence and used 2022 for the 24% stat.
